newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Czech Wood&Co buys 5.4 pct in big Ukrainian bank.
newsitem.headline: Czech Wood&Co buys 5.4 pct in big Ukrainian bank.

text.p: Czech brokers Wood and Company bought a 5.4 percent stake in Ukrainian commercial bank Ukrayina on December 3, a senior official from the brokerage said late on Wednesday.

Ivan Kompan told Reuters a deal for 1.8 million hryvnias was made on the Ukrainian Stock Exchange and one for 1.2 million hryvnias in electronic over-the-counter trading. These are the biggest single deals ever conducted on the two markets, he said.

The shares in Ukrayina, which is in the top three of Ukraine's 200 commercial banks, were sold at 10 percent above nominal value (0.01 hryvnia), Kompan, who heads the company's research department, said.
The head of shares and markets at Ukrayina, Yuri Lysenkov, told Reuters that Wood and Company had become the bank's biggest shareholder by acquiring 5.4 percent.
Authorised capital on June 1 was 46.74 million hryvnias (about $25 million) against 37.25 million hryvnias on January 1 and 8.75 million hryvnias a year earlier.

The bank is currently conducting a new share issue which began on October 15 and is due to end on March 31 and will raise authorised capital by 15 million hryvnias to 61.74 million (about $33 million).

The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is considering acquiring a 15-20 percent stake in the bank and the EBRD's board of directors is due to meet this month to decide whether to go ahead with the plan.
Kompan said Wood and Company had entered the Ukrainian market two months ago and saw it as one of the most promising.
"We have not registered our brokerage at the Ukrainian Stock Exchange yet but plan to do this very soon and create a company which will work here permanently," he said.
